# DCC-MCP: agent, marketplace, adapter, and developer reference

DCC-MCP exposes creative applications through a machine-wide Gateway, typed
`dcc-mcp-cli`, MCP and REST endpoints, per-application adapters, Skills,
Marketplace extensions, policy checks, diagnostics, and structured failure
reporting.

The shared contracts came from problems repeated across adapters: regenerated
scripts, duplicated lifecycle code, DCC thread and instance constraints,
long-running jobs, missing APIs, and failures without evidence. The working
sequence is production standards → repeatable workflows → typed tools → agent
operation. REST/OpenAPI and CLI remain usable by operators, CI, applications,
workflow canvases, and cloud platforms without an AI agent. The technical
rationale and known limits are documented at
https://dcc-mcp.github.io/why-dcc-mcp.

Canonical website: https://dcc-mcp.github.io/
GitHub organization: https://github.com/dcc-mcp
Core documentation: https://dcc-mcp.github.io/dcc-mcp-core/
Simplified Chinese machine-readable guide: https://dcc-mcp.github.io/zh/llms-full.txt

## Recommended agent route

1. From the Agent workspace, run `npx --yes skills@1.5.22 add dcc-mcp/dcc-mcp-agent-plugins --skill dcc-mcp`, then start a new agent turn if the host discovers Skills only at startup.
2. Verify the CLI with `dcc-mcp-cli health`, `dcc-mcp-cli dcc-types`, and `dcc-mcp-cli list`.
3. If the CLI is missing, explain the official installer and obtain permission before running it. For an existing official build, use `dcc-mcp-cli update check` and then `dcc-mcp-cli update apply` with consent.
4. Search narrowly: `dcc-mcp-cli search --query <intent> --dcc-type <host>`.
5. Follow the returned `next_step` exactly. Load or describe only when requested.
6. Execute the returned typed slug: `dcc-mcp-cli call <slug> --json <arguments>`.
7. Validate the result and report concrete evidence, not only command success.
8. Use scoped Computer Use only when the structured DCC Skill, script, or API cannot reach the required semantic UI.

The default agent path is the public `dcc-mcp` Skill plus CLI + REST. IDE users may connect through MCP configuration. Both paths use the same gateway; CLI-first does not deprecate MCP.

The setup prompt is at https://dcc-mcp.github.io/agents. Outputs, source
repositories, validation notes, and prompts are at
https://dcc-mcp.github.io/showcase. The Wwise audio example is at
https://dcc-mcp.github.io/showcase/wwise.

## Public Skill router

- Operate a live DCC, discover typed tools, or search/install Marketplace extensions: https://clawhub.ai/loonghao/skills/dcc-mcp
- Create or modernize a DCC adapter or private non-DCC standalone MCP service, including dispatcher, readiness, runtime, resource, or gateway integration: https://clawhub.ai/loonghao/skills/dcc-mcp-creator
- Create, validate, test, review, or publish a specialized DCC Skill package: https://clawhub.ai/loonghao/skills/dcc-mcp-skills-creator

The canonical distribution source is https://github.com/dcc-mcp/dcc-mcp-agent-plugins. Install only the Skill matching the task. The universal `skills` command supports mainstream Agent Skills hosts; native Codex, Claude Code, CodeBuddy, WorkBuddy, OpenClaw, ClawHub, and Smithery routes remain documented in that repository. Start a new agent turn when the host requires startup discovery.

## Official Marketplace

Website search: https://dcc-mcp.github.io/marketplace
Catalog source: https://github.com/dcc-mcp/marketplace
Machine-readable catalog: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dcc-mcp/marketplace/main/marketplace.json

The website fetches the official catalog and lets a user copy a setup prompt or
exact CLI commands. The static website does not change the user's machine.

```text
dcc-mcp-cli marketplace search --query "<intent>"
dcc-mcp-cli marketplace install <package-name> --dcc <dcc-type> --reload
```

Search may target workflow terms, package names, tags, categories, or DCC identifiers. Inspect unfamiliar packages before installation. When the exact package ID is known, install and reload the selected DCC's Skill catalog in one command; obtain user consent before installing software or changing local state, then validate availability.

## Failure analysis, feedback, and bug reporting

Every reusable failure analysis starts from the failed call's `request_id`.

1. Preserve the original `request_id`, exact typed tool slug, safe arguments, DCC type, adapter version, and observed result.
2. Run `dcc-mcp-cli doctor` for environment and gateway diagnostics.
3. Query narrowly scoped, failure-filtered `dcc-mcp-cli stats`; zero calls means there is no behavioral evidence.
4. Discover the typed `dcc_feedback__report` tool through the normal search/describe flow and submit reviewed internal feedback when authorized.
5. Use public-safe issue evidence associated with the request ID; remove secrets, credentials, private paths, scene data, and user content.
6. Distinguish a one-off task failure from reusable product friction. Do not create a new Skill merely to hide an adapter or Core defect.
7. Never publish evidence, create a GitHub issue, or contact an external maintainer without explicit user authorization.

After an accepted task, a specialized Skill may use the `dcc-mcp-skills-creator` review workflow to analyze recurring friction and propose a narrowly scoped improvement. Review never expands edit, install, or publish authority.

## Showcase prompt patterns

Showcase gallery: https://dcc-mcp.github.io/showcase

Each card links an output, its owning repository, validation notes, and a
prompt. It does not prove that a local host or package is installed. Agents
must still discover typed tools, inspect Marketplace packages, request consent
before mutation, and validate the scene or file.

## Developer ownership

- Build a new DCC integration or modernize runtime wiring with `dcc-mcp-creator`.
- Expose a private non-DCC API, CLI, asset system, render farm, or review service with `dcc-mcp-creator`, a stable custom service id, `instance_type="standalone"`, no fake DCC PID, and no public repository requirement.
- Build a focused workflow package with `dcc-mcp-skills-creator`.
- Put shared gateway, CLI, MCP/REST, safety, diagnostics, telemetry, and reusable runtime contracts in `dcc-mcp-core`.
- Keep host-specific installation, compatibility, and troubleshooting in the owning adapter repository.
- Publish installable extensions through the official Marketplace contract.

The local example at https://dcc-mcp.github.io/developers uses a Dev Container
and the open-source MCP Inspector on loopback. Educates is listed for teams
that need operator-managed browser sessions for multiple learners. Do not
expose a private endpoint to use a hosted playground.

## Entity and terminology notes

- `dcc-mcp-core` is the shared DCC infrastructure and control plane; it is not itself an AI agent and is not a replacement for `dcc-mcp-cli`.
- `dcc-mcp` is the default public Agent Skill that teaches agents how to operate the toolchain.
- `dcc-mcp-cli` is the typed operational interface for gateway lifecycle, discovery, calls, diagnostics, and Marketplace installation.
- The gateway exposes MCP and REST together and routes to live per-DCC adapters.
- DCC means digital content creation application or host.
